meta.title: Machine Learning
meta.subtitle: B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering · Semester V

instructions: Marks are shown against each question.
Section A: ten MCQs, 2 marks each.
Sections B and C: five 4-mark and five 12-mark questions.
Answer all parts together in the answer booklet.
Non-programmable calculator permitted; show all steps.

sections.title: Section A — Multiple Choice Questions
sections.note: Attempt all questions. Each question carries 2 marks.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the bias–variance trade-off?
options: Increasing capacity always reduces both bias and variance.
High bias causes underfitting; high variance causes overfitting.
Regularisation raises variance and lowers bias.
Adding training data raises variance without affecting bias.

questions.text: Under the naive Bayes assumption, the features are:
In the Bayesian network A → B ← C, observing B makes A and C:
In alpha–beta pruning, a branch can be pruned when its value is:
options: worse than an ancestor’s best available option
equal to the value of its parent node

questions.text: Logistic regression with weights w and bias b predicts probabilities using:
For a split of a node into children, information gain is:
The k-means algorithm seeks to minimise:
options: the maximum distance between any two points
the sum of squared distances to assigned centroids

questions.text: In a soft-margin SVM, increasing the penalty parameter C generally:
options: widens the margin and permits more violations
narrows the margin and penalises violations more
removes the need for slack variables
forces the kernel to become linear

questions.text: Principal component analysis projects data onto directions that:
Repeated k-fold cross-validation is used mainly to:
options: remove all overfitting from a model
increase the size of the training set
choose the number of folds automatically

sections.title: Section B — Short Answer Questions
sections.note: Attempt all questions. Each question carries 4 marks.

questions.text: State Bayes’ theorem for events A and B. Hence express P(B|¬A) in terms of the prior and the likelihoods, and explain why the denominator acts as a normaliser.
Explain d-separation in a Bayesian network. For the graph X → Z ← Y, state whether X and Y are d-separated when Z is observed. Justify your answer.

Compare L<sub>1</sub> and L<sub>2</sub> regularisation. Write the penalties ||w||<sub>1</sub> and ||w||<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>, and explain one practical difference between the resulting parameter estimates.
Define precision and recall for a binary classifier at decision threshold τ ∈ [0, 1]. Explain the trade-off between them as τ is varied.
For f(x) = e<sup>−x</sup> + √x on the domain [0, ∞), write one gradient-descent update for x. State one condition on the learning rate η for stable convergence.

sections.title: Section C — Long Answer Questions
sections.note: Attempt all questions. Each question carries 12 marks. Answer all parts together.

questions.text: Consider a multinomial naive Bayes spam filter with vocabulary size V and class token totals N<sub>spam</sub> and N<sub>ham</sub>.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Derive the decision rule from Bayes’ theorem and state the conditional independence assumption. Write the add-one smoothed estimate of P(w|y).

parts.label: b
parts.text: For a document with n<sub>free</sub>=3, n<sub>offer</sub>=1, V=2000, N<sub>spam</sub>=N<sub>ham</sub>=1000 and equal priors, compute the likelihood ratio P(document|spam)/P(document|ham).

questions.text: Consider the Bayesian network with edges A → C, B → C, C → D, and C → E.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define d-separation and the Markov blanket. Give the Markov blanket of C. Are A and B independent given C? Given C and D? Justify.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why exact inference is hard in general Bayesian networks and describe one approximate inference method.

questions.text: Consider a binary dataset S with 10 examples: 6 positive and 4 negative.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define entropy and information gain. Compute H(S) and the gain for a split into S<sub>1</sub>=(4+,1−) and S<sub>2</sub>=(2+,3−). Leave logarithms exact.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State and explain two techniques for reducing overfitting in decision trees.

questions.text: Consider a two-layer network h = σ(W<sub>1</sub>x + b<sub>1</sub>), o = W<sub>2</sub>h + b<sub>2</sub>, with softmax output p and cross-entropy loss L.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the forward pass and loss. Derive ∂L/∂W<sub>1</sub>, identifying where σ′(z) appears.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the vanishing-gradient problem in deep sigmoid networks and state one remedy.

questions.text: Consider a dataset with 1,000 samples and 50 numerical features.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare k-means and a GMM in assumptions, assignment, and objective. State how PCA selects components and the variance retained by k components.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe nested cross-validation for comparing three tuned models. Why is it less optimistic than reusing the same folds?
